summary: machine-readable report carried CJK text, and on Windows every consumer that pipes it turned the verdict into 'output was not JSON'
root_cause: The explainability fields were written in Chinese because the surrounding documentation is Chinese. The report is a pipe product: subprocess readers decode stdout with the platform default (cp936 here), not guaranteed UTF-8. Nothing in the code said which of the two audiences a field is for.
detection: tests/test_compare_sut_results and tests/test_decision_vectors failed with 'output was not JSON: ' while the same command printed valid JSON in a terminal. The difference was the decoder, not the verifier.
fix: Machine-readable fields are ASCII English; Chinese stays in the human-facing `uibc explain` text. Stated as a rule in uibc_core/explain.py's module docstring.
lesson: A report has two audiences with two encodings. Deciding per field which audience it serves is part of the schema, not a translation afterthought - and a CJK string in JSON is a portability defect that no unit test in-process can see.
